newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: UK wants bigger slice of future Falklands oil cash.
newsitem.headline: UK wants bigger slice of future Falklands oil cash.

text.p: Britain wants a bigger share of any future oil revenue from the Falkland Islands than the remote South Atlantic archipelago has offered so far, Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said on Friday.

Foreign oil companies are due to start full-scale exploration late this year and the islands' government has said that if oil is found, it would be prepared to pay Britain its annual defence costs of 65 million pounds ($110 million).

But Portillo told reporters this was not enough and made clear Britain would be pressing for more. Industry analysts say the oil reserves could total some three billion barrels. "This may seem paradoxical but we think it would be much easier to make an agreement before we know whether there is oil or not," Portillo said.

"What we would like to see is a formula agreed now. Our suggestion is we should have a formula which is not related to defence. It should bear some relation to what size the oil reserves turn out to be and how much revenue that generates."

The Falklands also offered to pay some of the 3.6 billion pounds ($6 billion) which Portillo said Britain had invested in boosting the islands' defence since fighting a brief war with Argentina over the archipelago in 1982.
On Thursday he told the 2,400 islanders that the government would not weaken their defences against Argentina despite improving ties with Buenos Aires.

The Falkland Islands government issued licences in October to a dozen companies operating in seven different tranches in waters north of the islands. The licences were won by consortia led by Amerada Hess, Royal Dutch/Shell, LASMO Plc, International Petroleum Corp and local firm Desire Petroleum.
